test_title: SSC MTS 2024 Official Paper (Held On: 05 Nov, 2024 Shift 1)
subject: general
question:
The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains an error.

I regret / in notify that / the model you want/ is out of stock.
solution:
The correct answer is **Option 4**.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The phrase "**in notify**" is grammatically incorrect.
 
• The correct expression should be "**to notify**" as the verb "regret" is followed by an infinitive ("to" + base verb) when expressing formal notification or announcements.
 
• Thus, the corrected sentence should be: "*I regret to notify that the model you want is out of stock.*"
 
• Therefore, the grammatical error lies in **segment 2**.

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 4**.

 

**Correct Sentence:** *"I regret **to notify** that the model you want is out of stock."*

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Use "**regret to + verb**" when expressing formal regret about an action you're doing now or about to do (e.g., regret to inform, regret to announce).
 
• Use "**regret + verb-ing**" when expressing sorrow about a past action (e.g., I regret saying that).
